text:
Ruben Amorim says that he is encouraged by what he sees from club record signing Goncalo Ramos despite his lack of goals, and says that he is pleased to see Francesco Camarda return from international duty ‘happier’ after a conversation with Italy U21s head coach Silvio Baldini.
Amorim spoke at length about his centre-forwards during his pre-match press conference ahead of Milan’s upcoming test against Frosinone on Sunday, which kicks off at 17.00 GMT.
This will be Milan’s first game back after the international break. The Rossoneri started the weekend in fourth place with 24 points from their first four matches and will face a tough test against the sixth-place Frosinone, who are just four points behind them.
Amorim’s pre-match press conference ahead of Frosinone vs. Milan
Talking to the media on Saturday, Amorim confirmed that he does not have any new injury concerns: “I think everyone is ready. We had to control the load during the week because some of the guys were travelling, but everyone is ready, the guys that are available. I’m really pleased with the players playing, because it’s the best way to maintain. We are ready for the game.”
Strahinja Pavlovic is a doubt, but Amorim confirmed that he will be part of the travelling squad at the very least on Sunday.
“Starting with Pavlovic, he’s doing better, he’s going to be in the squad. I don’t know if he’s going to start. I need to see. But he wants to play, I want him to play because we miss that fire that he has, I really like that. But we have other players that have been training more, so let’s see.”
Assessing the opposition, Amorim added: “Frosinone, for me, are fun to watch. The pace, they are the team that sprints the most and the pace of the team is really high. We are the second team for sprinting, so I think we are able to fight that.
“They’re really good one-on-one out wide. Watching Frosinone games, it’s hard to understand their movement because there is some logic in the chaos they bring, but it’s hard to understand.
“Compared to us, they are clearly better at getting the ball in the final third. They play a different style, it’s more direct, it’s more about where they win the ball and that allows them to have the ball more in the final third. They don’t think about preparing long plays. It’s going to be a really hard game.
“There are some teams where we have to be so focussed because that style can create a lot of problems. I expect a difficult game, but we also have our own ideas to create problems for the opponent.”
Amorim went on to speak in depth about the ‘struggles’ his centre-forwards have experienced this season.
Alphadjo Cisse, Adrien Rabiot, Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira have combined for 21 goals across all competitions so far this season, but club record signing Ramos and his understudy Camarda have only netted three between them, all of which have come from the Portugal international.
Amorim insists that if Ramos is struggling to find goals, it is because Milan are struggling to get him into the right areas.
He explained: “Of course, we can say that maybe one more option [in January] can be a good thing to help Camarda and Ramos, but I think that Ramos’s struggles are the struggles of the team. I had two weeks to understand the data that you guys have and I have. We are not reaching the final third, we are one of the worst teams at getting into the final third and continuing from there.
“We don’t have a lot of shots. I don’t want a team that takes a lot of shots from outside of the box, because most of the time you can’t score from outside the box. But we are not helping Ramos.
“In the game against Genoa, without Ramos, we don’t score the two goals. He didn’t score, but without Ramos, we don’t score those two goals.
“My biggest concern is the team, and it’s about the volume of the offence. We can’t continue like that. We are scoring many goals, but with less volume [of attacks]. But if you think we can maintain this with less volume and more goals, we are not going to be able to continue with that. So my goal is to push the team forwards, that is my job and not Ramos’s job.
“We need to push all of our players near the box, Ramos, Camarda, Pulisic, Rabiot, all these guys. Ramos is struggling because the team is struggling. But Ramos is a guy who follows the midfielder, the centre-back. I know that it’s not his job. I know that we’ve bought a player to score goals, but I’m not doing the [best] job to help Ramos, but Ramos is doing everything to help me and I know that Ramos is going to score many goals. But we need to push the team forwards for him to play in the position of a striker.”
As for Camarda, who has appeared for just 36 minutes in Serie A this season, Amorim said: “The important thing, it’s normal. I was a young player that wanted everything really fast and I think that happens with a player who really wants to play, and that is a good thing. I think he needs time to adapt at a different level. To play for Milan is really hard, it’s up to the guys who have the experience.
“He needs time to grow up, to feel settled at the club. I don’t know what’s going to happen in January. He needs to be focused on these next games. In football, everything can change in one week, so imagine until January. The focus is on the next training, the next game and anything can happen.
“I’m really pleased with the way he’s returned. Maybe because he’s changed his environment. I heard Mister Baldini had a conversation with him. I don’t know what he said to the kid, but he came [back] happier. I’m really pleased with Mister Baldini’s conversation with him and I’m happy for Camarda.

“But this can happen with kids in a big club, he just needs to focus on the next training, enjoy himself, then the next game and things are going to settle down. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away.”
Amorim went on to explain that Milan’s January transfer plans will not be affected by their position in the league table come January.
“That is the biggest mistake of the big clubs, looking at the table and thinking if you’re near, let’s invest, crazy investments. If we’re not near, let’s not invest. I think the key point is to have a long-term plan. If you lose all the games, sack the manager, that is normal, I’m not talking about that,” he laughed.
“What I’m saying is stick with your plan. We have a plan. What sort of player we want, someone who is able to make all the runs we want, who has the character we want, not a big star, a guy that is composed to be part of the team. If we have that really clear and we go for the best that we can, young or old – younger would be better – but if we have a clear plan, don’t look at the table. Look at the table to evaluate the process, but if you’re spending money for the next five years, don’t look at the table.”
